excerpt: ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 23/02/2022 (Innocent Ltd, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « Because the ads implied that purchasing Innocent products was a choice which would have a positive environmental impact when that was not the case we concluded that the ads were misleading »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 31/08/2022 (Unilever UK Ltd, publicité Persil, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « We concluded that the basis of the claim “kinder to our planet” had not been made clear » ; « We told Unilever UK Ltd t/a Persil to ensure that the basis of environmental claims was clear in future ads »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 29/11/2023 (Renault UK Ltd, publicité Dacia et Renault, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « The ad, therefore, omitted material information and was likely to mislead » ; « We told Renault UK Ltd to ensure that ads included all material information needed for consumers to understand their message and reminded them that the basis of environmental claims must be clear »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 07/02/2024 (BMW (UK) Ltd, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « we concluded "Zero Emissions Cars" was likely to mislead » ; « We told BMW (UK) Ltd to ensure that ads referring to “zero emissions”; made clear that the claim related to an electric vehicle only when it was being driven » ; « The basis of environmental claims must be clear »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 09/04/2025 (TotalEnergies SE, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « In the absence of that information, we concluded the ad was likely to mislead » ; « We told TotalEnergies SE to ensure their future ads that focused on environmental initiatives did not mislead by omitting material information about the proportion of their overall business activities that comprised lower-carbon activities »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 30/04/2025 (Lavazza Coffee (UK) Ltd, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « but as they were not intended to be placed there, we considered the claim was likely to mislead » ; « We told Lavazza Coffee (UK) Ltd to ensure their search ads did not mislead over the correct route for disposal when making composting claims » ; « The ad breached CAP Code (Edition 12) rules 3.1, 3.3 (Misleading advertising), 11.1, and 11.2 (Environmental claims) »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 03/12/2025 (Nike Retail BV, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « We therefore concluded the ad was likely to mislead » ; « We told Nike Retail BV t/a Nike to ensure that the basis of future environmental claims, and their meaning, was made clear »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 24/06/2026 (Uniqlo (UK) Ltd, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « We therefore concluded that the ad was likely to mislead » ; « We told UNIQLO Europe Ltd t/a UNIQLO to ensure that their future ads made the basis of any environmental claims clear and did not suggest that their products were entirely made from recycled materials when that was not the case »

ASA (Advertising Standards Authority, autorité britannique de régulation de la publicité), décision du 24/06/2026 (Adidas UK Ltd, plainte retenue, en anglais) : « We therefore concluded the ad was likely to mislead » ; « We told Adidas UK Ltd t/a adidas to ensure that their future ads made the basis of any environmental claims clear and did not suggest their running shoes or other products were entirely made from recycled materials when that was not the case »
